newsitem.title: USA: Away on Business: What really counts.
newsitem.headline: Away on Business: What really counts.

text.p: The frills are nice, but when it comes to business travel by air the three things that really count are getting there on time, checking in with ease and finding an airline with a work-friendly flight schedule.
That comes through in the latest survey of the travelling public in Frequent Flyer magazine.

The poll, conducted by J.D. Power and Associates and appearing in the magazine's June issue, found that the three factors mentioned accounted together for slightly more than half of what determines customer satisfaction with an airline.

Items such as food service, frequent flier programmes and in-flight activities each account for relatively little by themselves, though seating comfort weighs in as the fourth most important factor at 12 percent.

The same poll -- which was designed to reflect the market share of the nine major U.S. carriers -- found that Continental Airlines was rated tops for long-haul flights and second best for short-haul trips.
It marked the second year in a row that the Houston-based carrier took the top honours in the poll for long flights.
What's Continental doing right? We asked Sarah Anthony, a spokeswoman for the fifth-largest domestic carrier, who says Continental got there in part by listening to its customers.
"We have a 1-800 number for our customers, with operators who listen, take information, and we respond to it," she said. "Customers have direct access to corporate headquarters."
She also said Continental was the only airline last year that placed among the top three in four rating categories that the U.S. Department of Transportation releases monthly.
"In 1996, we ranked No. 1 for the fewest involuntarily denied boardings, No. 2 in on-time arrivals, No. 2 in baggage delivery and No. 3 in the fewest amount of complaints," she said.

"A few years ago, we instituted a pay-for-performance bonus. Eligible employees get a $100 bonus for on-time arrival every month we come in first in that category," she said. "We've been doing that for two years and it has contributed to overall customer satisfaction."

TWA, United, American and Southwest -- the last two tied -- rounded out the top five in the poll for best long-haul airline. For short-haul flights, America West came in No. 1, followed by Continental and U.S. Airways with Delta and Southwest tied for fourth.
